speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Government is considering or implementing regulatory sandboxes for small-scale carbon offsetting projects to identify and resolve the gaps including those around verification standards and the interface with the mainstream financial system; and (b) whether she can provide an update on the efforts to develop Singapore into a hub for carbon trading.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore is catalysing the development of credible carbon markets.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One is with regards to the efforts to develop Singapore into a hub for carbon trading.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As the Minister mentioned, there has been a multi-Ministry and Statutory Board effort, including efforts in terms of trading activity enhancements.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second question is, can we get the Minister's elaboration on the possibility of jobs creation in terms of carbon trading?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We are not the only country that wants to build up carbon trading to be a hub in the region.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think other countries, our neighbouring countries, would also want to build this up.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, how fast we can push these carbon trading efforts going forward?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: First of all, it is about our determination to be a hub for carbon trading.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We see carbon trading as part of the carbon services sector and also a part of the wider green economy growth that is very much part of our economic objectives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I cannot go into the specific situation that he has mentioned about what IRAS is doing, because that obviously is not within my Ministry's work, but I can assure him that we are working across many agencies and Ministries to develop the green economy, carbon services in general.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And similarly, when it comes to job creation, I am sure that we are also looking forward to more jobs for our people, but specifically, with regards to carbon trading, I would encourage him to ask the Parliamentary Question of our economic agencies.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, apologies for skipping your Parliamentary Question No 5 earlier.
